name: Syncope
description: Syncope is a transient, self-limited loss of consciousness caused by a sudden reduction in cerebral perfusion, typically lasting seconds to a few minutes with spontaneous full recovery. It is clinically distinct from other causes of collapse (e.g., seizure, hypoglycaemia) in that it is brief, non-convulsive, and followed by prompt orientation. Common causes include vasovagal (reflex) syncope, cardiac arrhythmias, structural heart disease (e.g., aortic stenosis), and orthostatic hypotension. Syncope during exertion or associated with palpitations is a red flag requiring urgent cardiac evaluation.
